subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add an agent-controlled pre-compaction lifecycle contract, and should that contract include warnings only, warnings plus structured handoff/checkpointing, or full bounded deferral?
rationale: The request crosses public config, session persistence, lifecycle hooks, and security boundaries because it can grant agents extra write opportunities and carry or block authority across a compaction boundary.

options.title: Warning and handoff only
options.body: Add a narrow opt-in warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path, while deferring agent-requested compaction delays until authority semantics are settled.

options.title: Full bounded deferral
options.body: Allow warning, handoff, and DEFER only with strict maximum duration, audit trail, idempotent checkpoint matching, approval expiry, and workspace/resource-scope validation.

options.title: Keep current surfaces
options.body: Decline a new core lifecycle surface and keep memoryFlush, notifyUser, hooks, compaction providers, and checkpoints as the supported extension points.

recommendation.title: Warning and handoff only
recommendation.body: Add a narrow opt-in warning plus structured handoff/checkpoint path, while deferring agent-requested compaction delays until authority semantics are settled.

likelyOwner.reason: The pre-compaction memory flush is the closest current lifecycle behavior and is central to deciding whether a structured handoff should exist.
